findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: The URL is hardcoded and not derived from untrusted input, so this is not a direct OS command injection vulnerability. However, if the URL were derived from user input, it could lead to OS command injection if not properly sanitized.
findings.assumptions: The URL is hardcoded and not derived from user input. The server at the URL does not execute shell commands based on the request content.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
findings.trigger: The email content is hardcoded and does not include any CRLF sequences. However, if the email content were derived from user input, it could lead to CRLF injection if not properly sanitized.
findings.assumptions: The email content is hardcoded and does not include any CRLF sequences. The server at the URL does not interpret the request content in a way that could be exploited by CRLF injection.

findings.title: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
findings.trigger: The email content is hardcoded and does not exceed the buffer size. However, if the email content were derived from user input and the buffer size were not properly checked, it could lead to a buffer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The email content is hardcoded and does not exceed the buffer size. The buffer size is properly checked using std::min(size * nmemb, email_data->size).
